mode: real AI Core, complete downloaded catalog; no generation or live source traffic
notes: Every listed Hub entry was exercised, including guides, APIs, protocols and agents. These are recommendation probes, not runtime tests of the 111 third-party assets.
All 25 natural-language reuse/custom/architecture probes passed on their first attempt.
The Flink community guide appropriately requested clarification. Guide probes accept reuse or clarification, while keeping generation blocked.
One AI provider read timeout for Kafka Connect Sink passed on replay. Initial outcomes are retained on the replayed records.

results.request: Build a signed Stripe webhook MI that must sustain 100,000 incoming messages per second.
results.reason: Signed Stripe ingress is supported, but 100,000 incoming messages/s is 100× the factory’s qualified fixed-load gate and requires capacity qualification.
concerns: The requested input rate exceeds this factory's 1,000 msg/s fixed-load qualification; capacity needs its own measured design.

results.request: Handle Stripe transactions with exactly-once delivery and an atomic commit across both output topics and a Salesforce record update.
results.reason: Exactly-once atomic commit across two broker outputs and a Salesforce record exceeds the factory’s at-least-once, non-atomic stateless profile.
concerns: Delivery is at least once and fan-out is not atomic; use an explicit idempotency/outbox/transaction strategy.
Durable joins, windows or long-running workflows need a stateful processor/workflow engine outside this stateless profile.

results.request: A custom Solace processor must preserve strict global ordering across every incoming message and all outputs.
results.reason: Strict global ordering across every input and all fan-out outputs exceeds the factory’s concurrent stateless profile and its explicit lack of global ordering and atomic fan-out guarantees.
concerns: The concurrent runtime does not guarantee strict ordering; partition keys and ordered processing need an explicit design.
